content: In #39932, the bot mentions no change to technical debt in the PR summary (neither strong nor weak). But the point of the PR is to remove a set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in. Is that expected?

This bug was introduced in mathlib-ci#28, and fixed in mathlib-ci#45.

(cc @Anne Baanen @Johan Commelin: I think we should make a habit of verifying that someone has asked an AI to review all CI changes before merging. mathlib-ci#28 had several other bugs, e.g. as fixed in mathlib-ci#36, and some further ones Claude+Codex just found now, in mathlib-ci#46.)

If humans cannot be trusted to adequately review the script (which I believe to be true for almost every nontrivial bash script I've seen), I think we're just wasting time and effort on trying to fix bugs incrementally.
I cannot test this script on my machine without various edits because it is not portable. What hope does a random user have to run it on their machine and trust the output?

(I weakly believe this also holds for all of our CI infrastructure. We've been getting away with it because we can test it somewhat adequately. But GitHub's current issues is making our experience so flakey I no longer trust testing either.)
To be clear, I regret that mathlib-ci#28 got merged in its current state and I should have been clearer that I could only do rudimentary tests.

I agree, it's rather hard to test CI scripts in a meaningful way before deployment, and hard to review just by staring at the code, and that's exactly why we should be using AI to both write and review them!

Well, not trying to understand code while writing or reviewing it would reduce my trust even further. But I think we come at this with sufficiently different values that trying to turn my modus tollens into your modus ponens or vice versa is going to waste time that we could both spend better. :)

Anne Baanen said:

If humans cannot be trusted to adequately review the script (which I believe to be true for almost every nontrivial bash script I've seen), I think we're just wasting time and effort on trying to fix bugs incrementally.

I strongly believe avoiding bash scripts will help, for both humans and AI, and both authors and reviewers.
I can volunteer to rewrite in Python or Lean if you agree.
Also we could use https://github.com/nektos/act to simulate CI locally. I've never tried it myself but I heard good things about it.

I would be very much in favour of a rewrite into Python, and can certainly try to help out with that project. (Lean might also work, but since this script does a lot of string manipulation, we might end up running into the limitations of the current string library.) Thanks for the offer!
